title: A Corner of Forty-Five Degrees
statement: Three of the $20$ vertices of a regular polygon with $20$ sides are chosen, and they are joined to form a triangle. For how many of the $\binom{20}{3}$ choices does the triangle have at least one angle of exactly $45^\circ$?
hints: All $20$ vertices lie on one circle. For each angle of the triangle, look at the arc between the other two vertices that does not contain the vertex of that angle.

An angle inscribed in a circle is half the angle that its arc makes at the centre. Each side of the polygon makes $18^\circ$ at the centre, so each angle of the triangle is $9^\circ$ times the number of sides of the polygon along the arc opposite it.

So an angle of $45^\circ$ means that two of the chosen vertices are $5$ sides apart, with the third vertex on the longer arc between them. Count these choices, then correct for the triangles in which this happens twice.
solution:
The vertices lie on a circle, and each side of the polygon subtends $18^\circ$ at its centre. If the chosen vertices cut the circle into arcs of $p$, $q$ and $r$ sides, then by the inscribed angle theorem the triangle has angles $9p^\circ$, $9q^\circ$ and $9r^\circ$. So it has an angle of $45^\circ$ exactly when one of these arcs has $5$ sides.

Each of the $20$ pairs of vertices $5$ sides apart gives such a triangle with each of the $14$ vertices strictly inside the other arc, of $15$ sides. There are $20$ triangles with arcs of $5$, $5$ and $10$ sides, one for each choice of the vertex between the two short arcs, and this counts them twice and every other triangle once. The answer is $20 \cdot 14 - 20 = 260$.

solution_figures.alt: A regular 20-sided polygon in its circle, with centre O. A triangle joins three of its vertices. Two of them are 5 sides apart, and the arc between them, made of 5 sides, is highlighted: it makes a right angle, 90 degrees, at O. The third vertex lies on the long arc, and the angle of the triangle there is 45 degrees, half of 90 degrees.
